spec.title: Clicks per service (rate)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_clicks_total) — per-instance: each instance counts only the clicks it served, so the panel sums across the selected instances to get the fleet total. Never max: that would report the busiest instance instead of the total.

spec.title: Clicks per service, role and target (total)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_clicks_total) — per-instance: each instance counts only the clicks it served, so the panel sums across the selected instances to get the fleet total. Never max: that would report the busiest instance instead of the total.

spec.title: Total Clicks
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_clicks_total) — per-instance: each instance counts only the clicks it served, so the panel sums across the selected instances to get the fleet total. Never max: that would report the busiest instance instead of the total.

spec.title: Favorites per service and role (top 10)
spec.description: Gauge (wolke_service_favorites) — shared state: every instance reads it from the one Postgres on its refresh, so all of them report the same number. The panel takes the max across the selection, which is that number. Never sum: that would multiply it by the instance count.

spec.title: Clicks per service and role (total)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_clicks_total) — per-instance: each instance counts only the clicks it served, so the panel sums across the selected instances to get the fleet total. Never max: that would report the busiest instance instead of the total.

spec.title: HTTP request latency p95 (by route)
spec.description: Per-instance histogram: each instance observes only its own requests, so the buckets sum across the selected instances before the quantile is taken.

spec.title: Active sessions
spec.description: Gauge (wolke_active_sessions) — shared state: every instance reads it from the one Postgres on its refresh, so all of them report the same number. Since #232 the metric carries a role label, so the total is max BY ROLE across the selection (the shared-state value for each role), summed across roles. A bare max would report the largest single role, not the total; a bare sum would multiply it by the instance count. Not filtered by the Role variable — this is the total.

spec.title: Catalog services
spec.description: Shared-state gauge: read from the one Postgres on every instance's refresh, so every instance reports the same value. Aggregated with max, not sum — summing would multiply the real number by the instance count.

spec.title: Active announcements by severity
spec.description: Shared-state gauge: read from the one Postgres on every instance's refresh, so every instance reports the same value. Aggregated with max, not sum — summing would multiply the real number by the instance count.

spec.title: Clicks per service in range (top 10)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_clicks_total) — per-instance: each instance counts only the clicks it served, so the panel sums across the selected instances to get the fleet total. Never max: that would report the busiest instance instead of the total.

spec.title: Favorites per service and role (current)
spec.description: Gauge (wolke_service_favorites) — shared state: every instance reads it from the one Postgres on its refresh, so all of them report the same number. The panel takes the max across the selection, which is that number. Never sum: that would multiply it by the instance count.

spec.title: Favorites added in range (top 10)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_favorites_added_total) — per-instance, so the panel sums across the selected instances. It counts only favorites users starred THEMSELVES: the role defaults pre-filled at first login are never counted, which is what makes this 'which services do people choose', not 'which services are favorited'. Read it next to the removed panel: a service that is starred and kept looks different from one that is starred and dropped again.

spec.title: Favorites removed in range (top 10)
spec.description: Counter (wolke_service_favorites_removed_total) — per-instance, so the panel sums across the selected instances. The companion to the added panel: a service high in both is one people try and drop again, a service high only in added is one they keep. A dropped role default IS counted here — dropping a pre-configured favorite is a user choice too.

spec.title: Active sessions by role
spec.description: Gauge (wolke_active_sessions) — shared state: every instance reads it from the one Postgres on its refresh, so all of them report the same number. The panel takes the max across the selection per role, which is that number. Never sum across instances: that would multiply it by the instance count. A configured role with nobody logged in reads 0 rather than dropping out, so a gap here means the exporter stopped.

spec.name: instance
spec.label: Instance
spec.description: Scrape targets to include. Counters sum across the selection; the shared-state gauges (read from the one Postgres, so every instance reports the same value) take the max instead.

spec.name: role
spec.label: Role
spec.description: Roles to include. They come from the deployment's OIDC claim mapping, so they are read off the metric rather than hardcoded here.
